haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store, uncharged.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive nightly days each under 0.1% mismatch, at least 5,000 invoices total. A person approves, and the rollback step must be none. The controller makes the move.
haiku-low.q4: Automatic trigger: charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only. Shadow new-engine errors never start a rollback.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only via Cutover. The gates reset, so the 7-day count restarts at shadow, and a person must approve forward moves again.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback from new_only stops being possible on day 35, when rollback edges are removed. The doc ties this to the 35-day event log but does not state the reason.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode and the rollback step before each new-engine charge; if the step is not none, they submit nothing. The doc does not say what happens to an invoice mid-processing.
haiku-low.q8: The rollout record holds the counters and Finance sign-off reference. The rollout controller refuses any forward move whose check fails, and needs person approval and no running rollback.
haiku-low.q9: NOT STATED which component measures the failure rate. The automatic trigger writes a rollback request naming the source mode to the rollout record, starting at Freeze.
haiku-low.q10: Charges falling due during rollback become open periods. They are charged at Cutover, once each, in the old engine's normal billing run, after a ledger key check.
haiku-low.q11: The idempotency key: both engines check the ledger before each charge. Freeze submits no new charges and checks submitted ones by key. Reconcile treats any period with a ledger charge row as done.
haiku-low.q12: The step is kept in the rollout record, and new-engine charges stay blocked. Steps can repeat safely, and the controller resumes from the recorded step; config outages resume when service returns.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store (never charged, never in the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging, so it stays current.
sonnet.q3: The gate to both must be met: 7 consecutive nightly comparison days, each with a mismatch rate under 0.1 percent, and at least 5,000 invoices compared across the 7 days. No rollback may be running (step is none). A person approves the move; the rollout controller checks the record and refuses if any check fails.
sonnet.q4: The automatic trigger starts it when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2 percent in any 10-minute window. It applies only in both and new_only. In shadow, new-engine errors never start a rollback.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, via Cutover. Before the new engine can take over again, the gates are reset (the nightly counter returns to zero and the 7-day count restarts at the next entry to shadow), the step is cleared to none, and a person must approve each forward move again, with each gate met.
sonnet.q6: On day 35 after entry to new_only, the rollback edges are removed. The document ties this to the 35-day clock and the usage event log's 35-day retention. It does not spell out the reason explicitly beyond that. billing_mode still reads new_only and the old engine may be decommissioned.
sonnet.q7: Workers read billing_mode (and the rollback step) from the config service before each new-engine charge. If the config service is unavailable they keep the last mode and step they read. NOT STATED for what happens to an invoice being processed at the moment the mode changes, apart from the rollback rules: charges already submitted are not resubmitted and are checked at the provider until final.
sonnet.q8: In the rollout record: the nightly counters and the Finance sign-off reference. The rollout controller checks the record and refuses the move if the gate is not met, if a rollback is running, or if no person has approved.
sonnet.q9: The document does not say which component does it (it is an open question). The automatic trigger measures the new engine's charge failure rate over any 10-minute window. When it is above 2 percent in both or new_only, it writes a rollback request to the rollout record, starting at Freeze, unless a rollback is already running (then it is only logged in the audit log).
sonnet.q10: A charge that comes due during the rollback becomes an open period (no charge row), and new-engine workers submit no new charges. It is actually made at Cutover, when the old engine's normal billing run charges each open period once, using its own invoice and checking the ledger for the key first.
sonnet.q11: The idempotency key (customer, billing period, invoice version) is checked in the ledger before each charge. A period with a charge row in the ledger is done and the old engine never charges it. If the provider shows a succeeded charge but the ledger has no row, Reconcile writes the row first. Verify checks that no period has two charge rows.
sonnet.q12: Billing is left in the rollback step recorded in the rollout record, with new-engine charges stopped and the rollback step not none. Each step can be repeated safely. Replay failure keeps the rollback in Replay and alerts. A Verify gap sends it back to Reconcile. If the config service is unavailable, the step is kept and resumed when it returns. The controller moves on only when a step's check passes. Not stated: what happens if the controller itself fails (it is not yet written).
